title: Mandarin grammar
intro: A working reference for beginners to intermediate learners. Chinese words never change their form: grammar lives in word order and in small particles. Read a section, notice the shape, then listen for it in what you watch and read.

sections.title: Basic word order
sections.text: Verbs don't change for person or tense: **我去 / 他去 / 我们去**. Time and place come **before** the verb, unlike English. **是** links two nouns (**我是老师**), but adjectives don't need it: **天气很好** (the weather is good), where **很** is often just a link, not "very".

head: Slot
Order
Example
rows: 我喝咖啡。 | I drink coffee.
我明天去北京。 | I'm going to Beijing tomorrow.
我在家工作。 | I work at home.
我每天在公司吃午饭。 | I eat lunch at the office every day.

examples.translation: He reads at the library in the evening.
examples.note: time and place before the verb

sections.title: Questions (吗, 呢, question words, A不A)
sections.text: The question word stays where the answer would go: **你去哪儿？ → 我去学校。** Use **几** for small numbers you expect (几个人？) and **多少** for larger or unknown amounts (多少钱？ how much?).

head: Type
Example
rows: 你忙不忙？ | Are you busy (or not)?
你叫什么名字？ | What's your name?
我很好，你呢？ | I'm fine, and you?
什么 | what ;; 谁 | who ;; 哪儿 / 哪里 | where ;; 几 / 多少 | how many ;; 怎么 | how ;; 为什么 | why

sections.title: Negation (不 vs. 没)
sections.text: **不** changes to the second tone before a fourth tone: **不是 búshì, 不对 búduì**. With 没 the 了 of a completed action disappears: **我吃了 → 我没吃**.

head: 不 bù
没 (有) méi (yǒu)
rows: 我不喝酒。 | I don't drink alcohol. ;; 明天不去。 | (I) won't go tomorrow.
我没去。 | I didn't go. ;; 我没有钱。 | I have no money.
是, adjectives in the present (say 不是, 不好)

examples.translation: I didn't go to work yesterday.

sections.title: Measure words (个, 本, 张…)
sections.text: A number or **这 / 那** (this / that) needs a measure word before the noun: **这个人, 那本书**. Two of something is **两**, not 二: **两个苹果**. When unsure, **个** is usually understood.

head: Measure word
Used for
Example
rows: 一杯咖啡 | a cup of coffee

examples.translation: I'd like two cups of tea.
How many siblings do you have?

sections.title: 了 (completion and change)
sections.text: 了 is not a past tense: habits and states in the past don't take it (**我以前住在上海** I used to live in Shanghai), and the future can: **你到了给我打电话** (call me when you've arrived).

head: Position
Meaning
Example
rows: 我买了一本书。 | I bought a book.
下雨了。 | It's started raining. ;; 我饿了。 | I'm hungry (now).
我学了两年中文了。 | I've been learning Chinese for two years (and still am).

sections.title: 过, 在, 着 (experience and ongoing actions)
sections.text: The negative of 过 is **没 … 过**: **我没吃过北京烤鸭** (I've never had Peking duck). 在 + verb can take 呢 at the end in speech: **他在睡觉呢**.

head: Marker
Meaning
Example
rows: 我去过中国。 | I've been to China.
a lasting state, or doing while
门开着。 | The door is open. ;; 他笑着说。 | He said with a smile.

examples.translation: Don't disturb him, he's in a meeting.

sections.title: 的, 得, 地 (all pronounced "de")
sections.text: Everything describing a noun comes **before** it, linked with 的, even whole clauses: **在银行工作的朋友** (a friend who works at a bank). With close relationships 的 is often dropped: **我妈妈, 我们公司**.

head: Character
Links
Example
rows: 我的书 | my book ;; 很贵的手机 | a very expensive phone ;; 我昨天买的衣服 | the clothes I bought yesterday
他说得很快。 | He speaks very fast.
她慢慢地走。 | She walks slowly.

sections.title: Want, can, should (想, 要, 会, 能, 可以, 应该)
sections.text: 会, 能 and 可以 all translate as "can": 会 for skills you learned, 能 for ability or circumstances, 可以 for permission. Negate with 不: **不会, 不能, 不可以**; but "don't have to" is **不用**.

head: Verb
Meaning
Example
rows: 我想喝水。 | I'd like to drink some water.
我要去银行。 | I need to go to the bank.
我会游泳。 | I can swim. ;; 明天会下雨。 | It will rain tomorrow.
你能帮我吗？ | Can you help me?
这里可以拍照吗？ | Can I take photos here?
你应该休息。 ;; 我得走了。 | I have to go.

examples.translation: I can't go today, I'm busy.

sections.title: The 把 construction
sections.rule: subject + 把 + object + verb + something more (result, direction, 了…).
sections.text: **把** moves a specific object before the verb to say what you do *to* it, especially when it ends up somewhere or in some state. The verb can't stand alone: it needs a result, direction or 了 after it.

head: Normal order
With 把
rows: 我关了门。 | I closed the door.
我把门关上了。 | I closed the door (shut).
请把那本书给我。 | Please give me that book.

examples.translation: I left my phone at home.

sections.title: Comparing (比, 没有…那么, 一样)
sections.text: Never put 很 in a 比 sentence (北京比上海很冷 is wrong); use 更 or an amount instead: **比上海更冷, 冷一点儿**.

head: Pattern
Example
rows: 北京比上海冷。 | Beijing is colder than Shanghai.
他比我高五厘米。 | He's 5 cm taller than me.
A 没有 B (那么) + adj
我没有他那么忙。 | I'm not as busy as him.
A 跟 B 一样 (+ adj)
我跟你一样大。 | I'm the same age as you.
最好 | the best ;; 更好 | even better

examples.translation: Taking the metro is faster than a taxi.

examples.text: 这个比那个便宜一点儿。
examples.translation: This one is a bit cheaper than that one.

examples.text: 这是我吃过的最好吃的饺子。
examples.translation: These are the best dumplings I've ever had.

sections.title: Linking ideas
sections.text: Chinese often uses both halves of a pair where English uses one word. **还是** is "or" in questions, **或者** in statements.

head: Pair
Meaning
Example
rows: 因为下雨，所以我们没去。
虽然 … 但是 / 可是 …
茶还是咖啡？ ;; 周六或者周日都可以。

examples.text: 虽然中文很难，但是很有意思。
examples.translation: Although Chinese is hard, it's very interesting.

examples.text: 如果明天下雨，我们就在家吧。
examples.translation: If it rains tomorrow, let's stay home.
He went home as soon as class ended.

sections.title: One-page memory map
points: Words never change form; meaning lives in order and particles.
No 是 before adjectives: 天气很好.
吗 makes a yes / no question; question words stay where the answer goes.
不 for present, habits and the future; 没 for the past and with 有.
Numbers and 这 / 那 need a measure word: 一本书, 这个人.
了 marks completion or change, not simply the past; 过 = have done before.
Describers come before the noun with 的: 我昨天买的书.
比 compares (no 很); 把 puts the object before the verb to say what happens to it.
sections.tip: Listening strategy: tones carry meaning (mǎi buy, mài sell), but context does most of the work. Listen for the small words that frame a sentence: 了 and 过 at the end, 吗 and 呢 for questions, and 不 / 没 for negation.
